key_insight: A spectrally regularized latent compression stage dramatically improves latent flow matching for turbulence by preserving dissipation-range structure that MSE-trained VAEs suppress.
engineering_relevance: The method delivers much higher-fidelity synthetic turbulence at low sampling cost, making it more practical for surrogate generation, reduced-order modeling, and data augmentation in CFD workflows.
method: Replace MSE-VAE compression with a zone-weighted log-spectral objective.
Train latent flow matching on the spectrally regularized latent space for unconditional turbulence generation.
Use encoder-decoder swap and support-amplitude decomposition to isolate where spectral gains originate.
evidence_signal: On a 256^2 DNS dataset at Re_f≈2250, deep-dissipation retained spectral power improved from 25% to 94% in reconstruction and from 20% to 79% in unconditional generation, with DD bias reaching -0.117 at 20 function evaluations.
watch_item: The paper reports a remaining deficit in the magnitude of S_3, so phase-coherent triadic organization may still limit full turbulence realism.
paper_title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation
